# Pandamonium v1.0.78

This train ships the rebuilt Entertainment shell. Installs with an AniCLI and/or PandaFlix plugin now get a branded full-screen streaming experience: a landing choice screen, anime and movies/shows browse pages with poster cards, real cover art, separate Favorites and Watchlist libraries, a Recently Watched resume tab, reliable long-session playback through the SSRF-safe media proxy, and an in-player Refresh/recovery control with the operator-supplied sound effects. No dependency, route-contract, schema, authentication, or stored-data change. Rollback remains signed v1.0.77 and the updater's retained pre-update snapshot.

## MAD-972 — Entertainment: branded streaming shell with cover art, libraries, and reliable playback

### Problem

The original Entertainment overlay was a small header, a plain hero, and flat result lists. It had no cover art, conflated Favorites with Watchlist, and offered no way to continue a show without searching for it again. Long-session playback stalled: the media proxy's opaque URL tokens had a 30-minute lifetime, but the preloaded next episode's tokens are minted a full episode early, so they expired mid-playback and every later segment returned 404 in a retry loop. Library clicks were a silent no-op whenever the clicked title's provider already matched the active one, because the collection view was never left. Autoplay advanced playback onto the preloaded `<video>` element, which had no `controls`, so the next episode could not be paused or seeked. The player also had no visible feedback for a refresh and no way to recover a stalled stream without reloading the page.

### Implementation

The overlay is rebuilt as the branded shell (top nav, sidebar, landing choice cards, anime and movies/shows browse pages, poster-card grid, player bar, footer) with the existing element ids preserved so search/resolve/play keep working. Cover art is resolved server-side by a new `POST /api/entertainment/metadata` and served through an owner-scoped, SSRF-safe `GET /api/entertainment/image/{token}` that only streams `image/*` under a byte cap and a one-day cache. Anime uses AniList; movies/shows use TMDB — the exact source PandaFlix is built on — with the TMDB key read at runtime from the installed PandaFlix extension source (or `PANDAMONIUM_TMDB_API_KEY`), falling back to TVMaze/Wikipedia with a relevance threshold so obscure titles show initials instead of a wrong poster. `prefs.watchlist` is a separate library with its own `＋/✓` card action and page; My Favorites keeps the star. A Recently Watched sidebar tab lists history entries with thumbnail, episode, and progress and resumes at the saved position. Proxy tokens gained a 12-hour lifetime plus sliding expiry so an actively-fetched stream cannot expire mid-playback. Library entries now always leave the collection view before resolving. `activateSlot()` moves `controls` to whichever stacked element is active so autoplayed episodes stay controllable. The player bar gained `⟳ Refresh`, which re-resolves the current stream at the current position with a disabled/"Refreshing…" state and a player-status line; fatal HLS network errors self-heal once. Open Pandaflix plays the operator-supplied `welcome-to-hollywood.mp3`.

### Product value and UI visibility

Operators and their installs get a streaming shell that looks like a product rather than a debug panel. Poster cards, Favorites and Watchlist as distinct libraries, and Recently Watched make the catalog browsable and resumable without re-searching. Playback survives a full binge: a preloaded next episode no longer expires, autoplay keeps its controls, and a stalled stream can be refreshed in place instead of losing the session to a page reload.

### Verification

Focused Python coverage for the entertainment routes, metadata resolvers (AniList batch/Page, TMDB year matching, Wikipedia relevance rejection, TVMaze scoring), the SSRF-safe image proxy (image-only, owner-scoped tokens, User-Agent), and sliding token expiry passed 23 tests. The Playwright entertainment suite passed 8/8, including new specs for Favorites/Watchlist separation, opening a library entry, autoplay target controls, and the Refresh progress feedback. Live acceptance on CT103 against the installed AniCLI/PandaFlix plugins: cover art resolved for the anime and "the blacklist" movie/show searches, the image proxy returned `200 image/jpeg`, autoplay kept controls, and Refresh re-resolved in place.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, schema, authentication, or stored-data change; the entertainment prefs shape only gains an additive `watchlist` array and per-entry `position`/`duration`, and older saved prefs remain valid. The optional `PANDAMONIUM_TMDB_API_KEY` environment variable overrides the TMDB key, which is otherwise read from the installed PandaFlix extension source and never committed. Metadata depends on public AniList, TMDB, TVMaze, and Wikipedia endpoints; when a source is unreachable or a title is not found, the card falls back to its initials rather than a wrong poster. Downloads and catalog browse pages (Genres/Popular/Top Rated/Recently Added) remain placeholders pending a catalog source.
